page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.16xlarge is a storage-dense, memory-optimized instance belonging to the Local SSDs family, deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 6763P-C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation stands at 512.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for workloads demanding extensive in-memory capacities.

A primary hardware feature of this instance is its direct inclusion of 30,717 GB of bundled local solid-state storage. For high-throughput communication across distributed nodes or storage architectures, the platform supplies a baseline network bandwidth of 160 Gbps. No graphics processing units (GPUs) are provided in this profile, concentrating its hardware allocation entirely on high-capacity memory, dense local disks, and multi-core CPU performance.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the ecs.i5e.16xlarge stems from its dense hardware aggregation, delivering immense local disk volume and high memory density within a single virtual machine boundary without requiring separate networked block volume attachments. It is particularly matched for large-scale distributed databases, Big Data analytics clusters, search index nodes, and extensive in-memory caching systems requiring fast local persistent storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5e.16xlarge is a dedicated KVM-based virtual server from the Local SSDs family, designed for dense data processing and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6763P-C processor clocked at 2.9 GHz, it supplies 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 512.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Its primary differentiator is the inclusion of 30,717 GB of local solid-state storage coupled with a high-capacity 160 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating without dedicated hardware GPU accelerators, the instance focuses compute and I/O resources on handling demanding local disk throughput and expansive memory structures. This hardware configuration is matched for large distributed databases, big data clusters, transactional datastores, and search engine infrastructure that require expansive local persistence and low-latency network interconnects.
